audience.programmeDescription: Erasmus combines mathematics, statistics, economics and programming to analyse economic questions and improve decisions. Students develop econometrics and optimisation methods, choose a major and complete a major seminar and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options combine substantial mathematical, statistical, computational and economic study. One emphasises economic models and optimisation; the other adds software, databases and predictive modelling. Erasmus provides a longer specialist econometrics sequence, dedicated time-series and mathematical-economics study, a major seminar and a required thesis. Shared rows show partial curricular relationships rather than identical courses or proof depth.

curriculum.limitation: The 12-EC minor and 12-EC elective spaces remain open within the School’s rules. The alternative 15-EC minor leaves 9 EC of electives.

componentNotes.b3-minor: 12 EC of approved minor study; an approved internship or exchange may replace it. No specific minor is assumed.
componentNotes.b3-major-seminar: Compulsory 12-EC forecasting seminar within the selected major. Entry requires completion of years one and two; attendance is compulsory.
componentNotes.b3-thesis: Compulsory 10-EC individual thesis on a subject from the major, after passing its seminar.
componentNotes.b3-career-future: This 1-EC career unit is distinct from the further 1-EC career elective. Career Skills normally requires at least 96 EC at the start of the academic year.
componentNotes.b1-intro-analysis: The first year also includes compulsory zero-credit Take-Off Bachelor and Guidance obligations. Attendance requirements apply; these add no EC to the degree.

cellNotes.text: Includes OLS, GLS and instrumental variables, statistical tests, Monte Carlo simulation in Stata and an empirical paper. It is one dedicated econometrics course.

concepts.label: Quantitative economics, econometrics & optimisation
concepts.concept: Mathematics, statistical inference and econometrics are combined with economics, programming, algorithms and computational optimisation to study quantitative economic and business problems.

concepts.label: Econometrics, data science & predictive modelling
concepts.concept: Mathematics, statistics and econometrics are combined with programming, software, databases, machine learning and neural networks, emphasising how data are organised and used to build predictive models.
